level1.process_type: femtosecond laser writing of buried type-II waveguides and single NV centres
level1.geometry_type: buried parallel modification-line waveguide with point NV-writing sites
level1.notes: Primary machining condition taken as waveguide writing: 230 fs, 515 nm, 500 kHz, 60 nJ, 0.5 mm/s; two modification lines are separated by 13 µm. The same setup also uses separate 28 nJ single-pulse exposures for NV formation. No fabrication focal-spot diameter is reported; the 9.5 µm value is the guided optical mode field diameter, not the writing spot.

level1.process_type: Bessel-beam laser writing / graphitization of conductive microelectrodes
level1.geometry_type: 500 µm-long transverse graphitic microwire through the diamond bulk
level1.notes: 20 Hz Ti:Sapphire source at 790 nm; experiments intentionally compare 200 fs and 10 ps regimes and multiple pulse energies. The Bessel central core is ~2.7 µm and all reported electrodes use 9000 pulses without sample translation. Total pulse energy does not uniquely specify energy in the Bessel core/rings, so a Gaussian-style peak fluence is not uniquely defined.

level1.process_type: femtosecond laser writing of stress-induced optical waveguides
level1.geometry_type: buried type-II waveguide formed by two parallel modification lines
level1.notes: 230 fs, 515 nm, 500 kHz, 100 nJ and 0.5 mm/s are explicitly reported for writing. A 1.25-NA objective is specified, but the fabrication spot diameter is not reported. The reported 10 µm mode-field diameter at 635 nm is a waveguide characterization result, not the writing spot.

level1.material_grade: synthetic single-crystal type-II optical-grade diamond (~100 ppb nitrogen)
level1.process_type: femtosecond laser writing of buried mid-IR type-II waveguides
level1.geometry_type: buried type-II waveguide with two parallel modification tracks
level1.notes: Fabrication uses 230 fs, 515 nm and 500 kHz with 0.5 mm/s scanning. Average writing power is deliberately varied over 75–100 mW and track separation over ~18–35 µm; the 2.4 µm and 8.6 µm wavelengths are characterization/guiding wavelengths, not fabrication wavelengths. No writing focal-spot diameter is reported.

level1.process_type: review of femtosecond laser micromachining of diamond
level1.geometry_type: multiple machining geometries and applications (review; no single processing geometry)
level1.notes: This is a review, not a single processing experiment. It compiles many laser systems, wavelengths, fluences, repetition rates and geometries from prior work; therefore no unique main processing condition can be assigned without selecting an external cited experiment.

level1.process_type: ultrashort-pulse laser drilling with heat-accumulation simulation and experimental validation
level1.notes: Validation drilling uses 228 fs, 514 nm, 25 µJ and a 13.6 µm spot. A 1 kHz condition is used for model-parameter experiments, while the main validation intentionally sweeps repetition rate up to 100 kHz; 50-pulse hole shapes are compared across conditions. No scan trajectory/hatch is used.

level1.process_type: excimer-laser percussion micro-drilling with optodynamic monitoring
level1.geometry_type: blind/through micro-hole produced by a pulse sequence
level1.notes: Processing laser: 308 nm, 20 ns, focal diameter 65 µm; fluence is swept over 16–30 J/cm² (21 J/cm² is a representative through-hole condition). Repetition rate is stated only as 'up to 20 Hz', so it is not a confirmed point operating value. Pulse number evolves through the drilling sequence.

paper_id: 4ae395a7cb947897_sc04_032_Efficient Water-Assisted Glass Cutting with 355 nm Picosecond Laser Pulses.pdf

level1.geometry_type: multi-line rastered cut-through kerf (~0.3 mm wide)
level1.notes: Primary condition taken as optimized low-power water-assisted cutting: 10±3 ps, 355 nm, 2.75 W, 529 kHz, 5.2 µJ, 6.1 J/cm², 600 mm/s and 10 µm hatch. The low-power condition uses the ~15 µm focused spot implied by the reported pulse energy/fluence and the stated spot options. The paper also contains an air condition and a separate 15.5 W high-power water regime. The minimum number of repeated scans is optimized but not tabulated as a single pass count.

paper_id: 3c0cf5859d4f9a93_Universal threshold for femtosecond laser ablation with oblique illumination.pdf

level1.material_grade: 1000 Å Au film on Si; soda-lime microscope slides; undoped single-crystal (100) Si
level1.geometry_type: isolated surface ablation craters at varied angle of incidence
level1.notes: 60 fs, 800 nm Ti:Sapphire source at 1 kHz; 18 µm 1/e² focal diameter. Pulse energy is deliberately varied and threshold fluence is measured as a function of material, angle and polarization. The stage translation is used to ensure single-shot ablation, but its actual processing speed/shot spacing is not reported (50 mm/s is only the stage maximum).

paper_id: 5b039bf3654767ec_Optimization of femtosecond laser processing in liquids.pdf

level1.process_type: ultrashort-pulse laser ablation of a metal in liquid; self-focusing/bubble optimization
level1.geometry_type: scanned surface ablation track/spot under liquid
level1.notes: For the solid-target bubble/ablation experiments, the paper reports 15 µJ pulses stretched to 1.5 ps, 1 kHz, 180 µm/s and a representative fluence of 2.7 J/cm² on polished Cu. The target-ablation wavelength is not stated. Separate liquid-only self-focusing experiments use an 800 nm source with minimum 35 fs pulses and should not be confused with the Cu processing condition.

paper_id: 86ddae97eec55fb0_Femtosecond Laser Processing of Germanium_ An Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics Study.pdf

level1.material_grade: diamond-cubic crystalline Ge (64-atom periodic simulation cell)
level1.process_type: ab initio molecular-dynamics simulation of femtosecond laser irradiation / phase transition
level1.geometry_type: bulk periodic atomistic simulation cell; no machined feature geometry
level1.notes: No physical laser beam wavelength, repetition rate, spot size or scan condition is specified. The ~100 fs excitation is modeled by elevating electron temperature. Table 1 maps seven simulation cases to incident fluences 0.0442–0.1325 J/cm² and corresponding intensities; these are a sweep rather than one processing point.
